correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md blob ef38425d0615591b5d9b0dfd02a37859b224ff84 and exact-corner source checker, and relevant source Gaur Lemmas 4,6,7. With axial cell centers S and P=conv(S), area(P+H)=area(P)+1+(w1+w2+w3)/3. For any spanning tree edge-count triple a+b+c=s=n−1, previous Gaur inequalities give U=(ab+bc+ca)−2area(P)≥0 and V=3s+max(a,b,c)−W≥0, both integers. Hence six times area equals L−3U−2V with L=3(ab+bc+ca)+6+6s+2max(a,b,c). For n=3k+2, maximizing remaining products shows each L is either N*=6M or at most N*−3. At L=N*, deficit 3U+2V cannot be 1, forcing any nonoptimal area at most M−1/3; in other residues simple six-area integrality limits deficit to at least 1. Three-segment connected path of cells with explicit (a,b,c) triples yields equality in each residue, with corner-hull formula. Independent exact integer optimization for all direction triples through n=89 and each witness family checks expected gap. No full area spectrum or shape stability is claimed.

value.rationale: This answers the first natural discrete stability question left open after finding the maximal convex-hull area for connected polyhexes: the smallest nonzero area deficit and why the first discrete level is forbidden at one residue. The sharp modulation and explicit near-optimal families are useful data for the broader, still-open attainable spectrum, not a routine restatement of Gaur’s maximum.

final_claim: For every n>=3 edge-connected array of n unit-area regular hexagons, the runner-up convex-hull area is M(n)−1/6 when n≡0,1 (mod 3), and M(n)−1/3 when n≡2 (mod 3), where M(n)=ceil(n²+14n/3)/6. No intermediate M−1/6 value exists in residue two; all runner-up values have explicit three-run witnesses.
